HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Medium-wide, low three-quarter angle across the lotus-lit palace pond at night. A loose ring of people around one grieving man: Chunchu stands at the center of the frame on the stone shore, arm in a sling, staring at the water; close beside him, his elderly mother Chunmyung, small and upright in purple silk; at the water's edge to the left, Queen Sunduk in her gold crown and red robe crouches beside Munhee, who holds a single paper lotus in both hands; in the background on the granite pavilion steps, a broad man in blue (Yushin) sits waiting; a little apart by the garden wall, a quiet princess in pale green with her hands folded (Seungman). Hundreds of paper lotus lamps on the black water as warm bokeh; a giwa pavilion behind. ONE device: the ring of figures around Chunchu. Crowded with love, everybody near him. One key: the candlelight from the water lighting faces from below. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = chunchu, SECOND face = sunduk, THIRD face = munhee, FOURTH face = chunmyung; the tile after the faces is an object reference (the Silla gold crown Queen Sunduk wears: copy this exact crown onto Sunduk's head — broad sheet-gold band, three tall tree-shaped uprights stepped like 出 with heart-shaped tips, two antler uprights at the sides, round gold spangles, pale-green jade gogok, two long gold pendant chains at the temples. Never a tiara, never a European crown). Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. KIM CHUNCHU — Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Colour #D8258C. QUEEN SUNDUK — Look: Pale oval face, dark calm eyes; black hair in a full coiled updo; when crowned, the gold Silla tree-and-antler crown hung with jade gogok. Dress: Crimson court robe with gold phoenix brocade, blue embroidered cape-collar, a red ribbon bow at the chest. Crown: Silla gold crown, copied from the attached Cheonmachong museum photo: a broad sheet-gold band with three tall tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 (three tiers of short arms turned up into heart-shaped tips) and two antler uprights at the sides, hung with hundreds of round gold spangles on wires and many curved pale-green jade gogok, two long chains of gold leaf pendants falling from the temples to the collarbones. Thin bright sheet gold, never a European spiked crown, never a solid cast crown or a tiara. Colour #E8552B. MUNHEE Colour #E07FA8. PRINCESS CHUNMYUNG Colour #d8a0e8. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
